chunks: Then it is said to the one who opposed us in that matter and insisted on its non-existence on the grounds of his occultation:

Why is it not permissible that Allah, the Exalted, enacts the obligation of knowledge (belief) and does not establish a sign/proof for it, if He knows that we do not consider it? Until, when He knows from our condition that we intend to consider it and are determined to do so, He creates the proofs and establishes them. At that time, we consider and say: What is the difference between an established proof that we do not consider, and its non-existence, until when we are determined to consider it, Allah, the Exalted, creates it?
ai.seo_question: What is the theological justification for the Imam's occultation based on divine knowledge of human intent?
ai.summary: Al-Tusi employs a dialectical argument to address the objection that God's concealment of the Imam renders the command to know Him futile. He posits that divine proofs are contingent upon human readiness, suggesting that God provides clear evidence only when the seeker is genuinely resolved to engage in intellectual scrutiny, thereby aligning divine wisdom with human agency.
